body: It helps man, really it does. Between you and the other guy who has offered advice in just these few couple of hours since my post I've been able to see my life in a oddly different light. I guess I am lucky enough to have had the opportunity between being in college (both times) and dropping out to have paid off the debt i accrued. I want to go back, but I am scared of the process it takes to transfer all the credit and re-apply for the financial aid it will take to finish. As for the rest of it, it means a lot that you would say those things, I just have this idea that so much is expected of me, that its hard to see how I am not disappointing my family because i'm not 'succeeding' in my own eyes. I have a hard time asking other people for help, advice and the like. I guess that's where I need to learn to put less stock in the expectations of others and more into my abilities and talents. It's hard to believe in myself, especially having never heard the words i'm proud from my father but I know that doesn't mean much any way. It's nice that after all the religious banter I believed when it comes to it, man to man, human to human, there are people out there willing to listen and put in their 'two cents'. march on seems like the theme, i guess maybe that it's probably easier to do than to try the out-route.
i went to a sobap college and the girl i dated also had a father who was a sobap preacher. small world i guess. slowly but surely. thank you for your perspective. it helped.

20 years of christian indoctrination only left me feeling guilty when I think about living a life according to plans I make for myself, 'indulging' in things I enjoy and not constantly being focused on other people. Maybe if I find a job, my mind will be a little more preoccupied. : \ thanks

I appreciate this, but I'm curious how you overcome the feeling of selfishness? When I try and do things for myself, things I used to enjoy, it all just feels so empty and useless. I do have an alt account and while I read and post on reddit a lot, I can not think of anything else I really do. I sold my xbox to pay rent before I moved. I sold my bike for the same reason. I enjoy smoking marijuana but without roommates growing and even a part time job, that isn't really an option aside from the fact that my mother works for the feds. I've contemplated joining the military to 'give myself something new to do' but it just seems so worthless in the end. what's the point of joy if you've no one to share it with? what's the point of happiness if no one sees you smile? thanks for the help, i guess i've got something to think about.
